If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast by 2–4% for late horizon (16–30 days) to correct for sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon to align with mean reversion.  
If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for mid horizon to offset bearish bias.  
If sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67) and forecast is volatile, apply 1–2% smoothing correction across all horizons to dampen noise.
